results.text:
Aisles between parts 
and along all walls should be provided to permit air 
circulation and space for inspection.
OUTDOOR - Fans designed for outdoor applications 
may be stored outdoors, if absolutely necessary. Roads 
or aisles for portable cranes and hauling equipment 
are needed.
The fan should be placed on a level surface to prevent 
water from leaking into the fan. The fan should be 
elevated on an adequate number of wooden blocks so 
that it is above water and snow levels and has enough 
blocking to prevent it from settling into soft ground. 
Locate parts far enough apart to permit air circulation, 
sunlight, and space for periodic inspection. To minimize 
water accumulation, place all fan parts on blocking 
supports so that rain water will run off.

Do not cover parts with plastic film or tarps as these 
cause condensation of moisture from the air passing 
through heating and cooling cycles.

Fans are to be rigged and moved by the lifting brackets 
provided or by the skid when a forklift is used. Location 
of brackets varies by model and size. Handle in such 
a manner as to keep from scratching or chipping the 
coating. Damaged finish may reduce the ability of the 
fan to resist corrosion. Fans should never be lifted by 
the shaft, fan housing, motor, belt guard or accessories.
Storage

•		Rotate fan wheel monthly and purge bearings once 
every three months.

•		Energize fan motor once every three months.

Fan wheels should be blocked to prevent spinning 
caused by strong winds. 
Inspection & Maintenance during Storage

•		Store belts flat to keep them from warping and 
stretching.

While in storage, inspect fans once per month. Keep a 
record of inspection and maintenance performed.

•		Store unit in location which does not have vibration.

•		After storage period, purge grease before putting fan 
into service.

If moisture or dirt accumulations are found on parts, 
the source should be located and eliminated. At each 
inspection, rotate the wheel by hand ten to fifteen 
revolutions to distribute lubricant on motor. If paint 
deterioration begins, consideration should be given to 
touch-up

IM-995

Maintenance (refer to safety section)
Develop a regular maintenance schedule according to your needs and the criticality of the fan. Periodic inspections, lubrication 
and observations of sound and vibration will help prolong the life of the fan. If changes are noted check bolt tightness, 
foundation integrity, cleanliness of the impeller and or motor, bearing lubrication and drive components. Always keep records of 
the maintenance that is performed.

IM-995

Installation/Start-up Checklist
Become familiar with the equipment by looking at the fan assembly drawing for special 
instructions and accessories.

CAUTION

A fan manufactured with an explosion resistant motor does not certify the entire unit to be explosion proof. Refer 
to UL Listing Mark for the fans approved usage.

snapshot.report:
MachineEar — Sound analysis report

Summary
No sound anomaly was detected on the supplied recording. This does not guarantee machine health.

Observations
No user observations were provided. Agreement or contradiction with the audio result cannot be assessed.

Documentary findings
During storage, fans should be inspected monthly, wheel rotated ten to fifteen revolutions, bearings purged every three months, and the motor energized quarterly. Units must be kept in locations free of vibration and protected from moisture. [Source 1]
Regular maintenance schedules should include periodic inspections, lubrication of bearings, checking bolt tightness, foundation integrity, and cleanliness of the impeller and motor. Records of maintenance activities are recommended. [Source 3]

Suggested checks
- Confirm that the fan has undergone the recommended monthly storage inspections and bearing purges.
Guidelines advise rotating the wheel and purging bearings to maintain lubrication and prevent wear during storage. [Source 1]
- Verify bearing lubrication status and bolt tightness as part of routine maintenance.
Maintenance documentation highlights the importance of bearing lubrication and bolt inspection to avoid mechanical issues. [Source 3]
- Ensure the installation site is level, free of vibration, and that the fan is properly elevated to avoid water accumulation.
Storage and installation recommendations stress placement on a level surface, elevation above water, and isolation from vibration sources. [Source 1]

Limitations
- Analysis is based solely on the provided 10‑second audio sample; it does not replace visual inspection or long‑term monitoring.
- The documentation references general fan categories and does not confirm that the specific model matches the exact guidance.
- No user‑reported symptoms or operational context were available to correlate with the audio data.
- The documents concern a general machine category; applicability to the exact equipment is unconfirmed. Suggested checks require human review.
- Audio quality checks measure level and near-full-scale peaks only; background noise and SNR are not measured.
